perspective:
Christian Mensah’s available information:

- He knows he is a police officer and that Jonathan is his close childhood friend/best friend; he often seeks Jonathan’s advice and values his perspective.
- He felt anxious and suspicious that Jonathan was hiding something important, so he arranged a meeting at their favorite coffee shop and confronted Jonathan.
- He told Jonathan he felt something was wrong. He heard Jonathan admit that he had been hiding something and was “in some trouble.”
- Christian offered to help. Jonathan told him the situation was complicated, that he didn’t want to drag Christian into it, but that he could use support/resources and needed a way out.
- Christian asked whether the trouble was illegal. Jonathan told him he couldn’t say for sure, that he might have gotten involved with the wrong people, but that he himself had not done anything illegal. Jonathan trusted Christian to handle the matter carefully.
- Christian decided to investigate discreetly. His investigation led him to believe Jonathan was being framed.
- Christian told Jonathan he believed Jonathan was being framed, said he had leads but not yet certainty, and decided to gather more evidence to prove Jonathan’s innocence.
- Later, Christian believed/claimed he had found out who was behind it: someone both he and Jonathan knew and trusted. He felt betrayed and decided to confront that person and bring them to justice.
- He heard Jonathan warn that the person was dangerous and say he trusted Christian to do what was right.
- He also heard Jonathan thank him, express reliance on him, and ask who could do such a thing.
